thread:
alexa: quick follow-up from today's RFC review — proposal: replace long-lived VPC peering entries for private control-plane egress with short-lived signed leases (ephemeral auth blobs). reduces Cardinality and simplifies ops. anyone see a blocker?

jordan: curious — signed leases sounds good. how do we prevent replay or stolen-lease abuse?

alexa: plan: leases are signed JSON with lease_id, tenant_id, allowed_cidrs, expires_at, and signer_kid. short TTL (usually 1-5m). dataplane verifies sig + expiry locally. replay window limited by TTL, and we provide a revocation endpoint for emergencies.

ryan: verifying signatures on dataplane — ok if we cache pubkeys. don't want per-connection mTLS.

alexa: exactly. dataplane fetches /operator/v1/jwks and caches keys with expiry. signer_kid allows rotation. verification is an in-memory check per lease, not per TCP flow.

sylvie: key rotation edgecases? what if jwks fetch fails?

alexa: fallback behavior: 1) use cached keys, 2) fallback to legacy peering mode if enabled via config flag, 3) if neither available, deny new egress allocations and surface alert.

kevin: migration story? ops rollback?

alexa: migration steps:
- roll out lease-issuer service in parallel with peering writes
- start issuing leases but keep peering reads as default
- flip a feature flag to prefer leases for read path (canary 1 region)
- monitor success metrics for 2 weeks, then stop peering writes
rollback: flip feature flag back to peering reads and pause lease issuance.

jordan: does this change our NAT/source-ip preservation guarantees?

alexa: lease includes preserve_source boolean. if true, operator allocates an ephemeral IP from tenant pool and records mapping in audit log. on failover we reprovision same IP if available.

ryan: storage/scale concerns — millions of short leases. need to avoid hot DB writes.

alexa: not all leases are persisted in hot DB. model: append-only audit log (cold, TTL-indexed) for compliance + small in-memory cache in operator for active leases. dataplanes maintain LRU of recent leases by lease_id. full historical persistence is in cold store for audits.

sylvie: reconcile flow for dataplane restarts?

alexa: dataplane startup flow: 1) fetch /operator/v1/leases?since=<cursor> to stream new leases 2) if cursor not found, full fetch with pagination. also a fast-path GET /operator/v1/leases/<lease_id> for synchronous misses.

kevin: can we see a sample lease and the operator API surface (conceptual)? also need a snippet showing how to flip back to legacy peering on incident.

alexa: sample lease (stringified JSON inside chat):
{
  "lease_id": "lease-ln-9f1b2",
  "tenant_id": "t-acme",
  "allowed_cidrs": ["10.10.8.0/24"],
  "expires_at": "2026-05-01T15:22:30Z",
  "preserve_source": true,
  "signer_kid": "cp-jwk-2026-04",
  "sig": "BASE64_SIG"
}

operator API (concept):
POST /operator/v1/leases -> 201 { lease_id }
GET /operator/v1/leases?since=cursor&page_size=1000 -> 200 [{lease}, ...]
GET /operator/v1/leases/<lease_id> -> 200 {lease}
GET /operator/v1/jwks -> 200 {keys}
POST /operator/v1/revocations -> 200 {revoked_ids}

fallback config example for dataplane (ops):
- feature flag: use_leases_for_egress = true
- if set to false, dataplane reads from legacy peering table and ignores leases
- on incident: flip flag to false in region -> immediate readpath fallback

ryan: two operational concerns: 1) revocation list size during mass incidents, 2) cold-start latency for first-miss when dataplane lacks lease.

alexa: counters: revoke list will be small if TTL is short; still add alert if size > threshold. cold-start: dataplane will synchronously GET /leases/<id> as a fast path; we should benchmark the p99. Also consider allowing a tiny permissive fallback policy for low-risk flows while verifying.

sylvie: metrics needed: lease_issuance_rate, lease_verify_latency_ms, jwks_fetch_errors, reconcile_lag_seconds, revocation_list_size, fallback_to_peering_count. also SLOs for jwks TTLs.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: lease-issuer canary scheduled 2026-05-03T09:30:00Z UTC.

kevin: i'll draft the rollout playbook and safe abort checklist. will add perf harness to simulate 100k leases/sec + jwks churn to validate cache behavior.

alexa: thanks — i'll write RFC addendum with schema, endpoints, migration/playbook + incident flip snippet. target: share spike results in next arch sync. :+1:

jordan: +1 from me, add a short runbook entry for oncall with the config flip commands and checks.

alexa: will do. closing this thread for now, will post RFC addendum link when ready.
